surprises.head: Washington couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: Washington usually gets some of the league’s most dangerous shots. Not tonight: a 4.6% chance of scoring on the average shot at 5-on-5, against their usual 7.1% (about 6.9% against New Jersey) and a league average of 6.4%. A team strays this far about once every 45 games.

story.head: Hellebuyck wins his first six, a Devils record
paras: Vladislav Kolyachonok made his Devils debut, after playing for the Bruins. Evan Rodrigues got the scoring started for the Devils on the power play early in the first. Ryan Leonard tied it 1-1 for Washington on the power play midway through the period. Pierre-Luc Dubois put the Capitals up 2-1 early in the second, but they didn’t score again. Lenni Hämeenaho made it 2-2 for New Jersey midway through the period, in his first game of the season. New Jersey had a goal taken off after a video review early in the third, but it didn’t cost them in the end. Kolyachonok put the Devils up 3-2 early in the period. Stefan Noesen made it 4-2 with just under three minutes left, and that was that. Jack Hughes added an empty-net goal with 45 seconds left to make it 5-2.

The chances were closer than the score. Connor Hellebuyck made 26 saves for the Devils, and Logan Thompson stopped 24 of 28 at the other end. Hellebuyck has won all six of his starts this season, the longest winning run to open a season by any goalie in franchise history, one more than Craig Billington (1991-92), Chris Terreri (1993-94), Akira Schmid (2022-23) and Jake Allen (2025-26). The Devils improved to 14-6-0, second in the Metropolitan, while the Capitals fell to 10-7-0, fourth in the Metropolitan.
